title: Sell Mineral Rights in Redstone, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Redstone, MT
metaDescription: Redstone, MT sits on the far western Bakken flank in Sheridan County, where activity has always been thin. I buy mineral interests here honestly.
heroLead: Redstone sits about as far west into Sheridan County's Bakken extension as the play reaches, and I tell people that plainly before we talk numbers.
intro: This is genuinely edge-of-edge ground. Redstone sits toward the western part of Sheridan County, past where most of the Bakken-era horizontal drilling concentrated, and the mineral interests I see out here are mostly old, mostly unleased, and mostly tied to homestead-era severances rather than any recent oil and gas activity. I'd rather set that expectation from the first phone call than let a family assume Redstone shares the same picture as Plentywood or Medicine Lake.
None of that means I won't take the call seriously. It just means the conversation starts from a different baseline than it would for a parcel closer to the state line.

sections.heading: Why the western flank thins out
paragraphs: Net pay in the Bakken and Three Forks generally decreases moving west and north away from the basin's depocenter in North Dakota, and Redstone sits far enough out on that trend that operators have had less economic incentive to drill here compared to ground closer to the state line. That's basin geology, not a knock on the area.

sections.heading: What I still check before quoting
paragraphs: Even on quiet ground like this, I pull the recorded chain from the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood, confirm the legal description, and check for any lease of record, old or current, before I say what an interest here is worth.

sections.heading: Why I don't discourage a family from calling anyway
paragraphs: A thin drilling record doesn't mean a worthless interest, and I'd rather do the work to give you an honest number than tell you not to bother. Plenty of families have real, sellable assets in ground exactly like this, just priced differently than acreage closer to the state line.

faqs.question: Is there any real chance of drilling near Redstone?
faqs.answer: Lower than in the eastern part of the county, given how the Bakken's net pay thins moving west. I evaluate your interest against that honest reality.

faqs.question: My family's minerals near Redstone have never been leased — is that unusual?
faqs.answer: No, that's the typical situation for this part of the county. I still buy these interests, priced as long-term potential.

faqs.question: How do you verify a Redstone-area parcel?
faqs.answer: Through the recorded deed chain at the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood, the same process I use countywide.

faqs.question: Is it worth checking if I'm not sure my family still owns anything out there?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give me what you have — even a rough family name and area — and I'll confirm through the county record before we go further.

faqs.question: Will you tell me honestly if it's not worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Yes. I'd rather tell you the real picture up front than waste your time chasing a number that won't hold up.
